title: Killing Two Birds with One Stone: Cross-modal Reinforced Prompting for Graph and Language Tasks

problem.claim: A generic framework is needed for learning across graph and language domains.

gap.claim: Existing work largely targets single-domain scenarios, while multimodal knowledge bridging and useful-knowledge selection remain challenging.

contributions.claim: A plug-and-play framework incorporates lightweight cross-domain prompting into graph and language learning tasks.
A domain-scalable prompt preserves textual semantics and logic while highlighting related graph information as external knowledge.
Reinforcement learning selects useful knowledge through an edge-selection strategy, supplemented by joint multi-view optimization for cross-domain collaborative learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present their framework as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments over 23 public and synthetic datasets reportedly show improved accuracy, robustness, and reasonableness across diverse multi-domain tasks.
The authors report improved performance for state-of-the-art graph and language models across different learning paradigms.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs and LLMs are capable in graph and language tasks, motivating cross-modal integration.
Prior studies focus mainly on single-domain settings, and cross-modal knowledge bridging and noise control pose challenges.
The framework uses scalable prompting, reinforcement-learning-based edge selection, and joint multi-view optimization.
The authors report broad empirical improvements across 23 public and synthetic datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative performance differences.
The abstract does not describe the reinforcement-learning algorithm, edge-selection policy, or optimization details.
